t:
Clauses (1) and (2) of subsection (b) of section 115 of title 23, United States Code, are redesignated as (A) and (B), respectively, including any references thereto. Such subsection (b) is further amended by inserting “(1)” immediately after “(b)” and by adding at the end thereof the following new paragraph:


“(2) 
For any project under construction on January 1, 1978, on the Interstate System and converted to a regularly funded project after January 1, 1978, for which the proceeds of bonds issued by the State, county, city, or other political subdivision of the State were used, any interest earned and payable on such bonds by the date of conversion is an eligible cost of construction, to the extent that the proceeds of such bonds have actually been expended in the construction of such projects.”.

fable.w: This section only redesignates clauses and makes bond interest on certain Interstate System projects an eligible construction cost. The tempting reading is that the mention of bonds issued by a State, county, city, or other political subdivision signals state or local involvement. That fails because those entities are named only as bond issuers whose costs may be reimbursed; there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue tied to a federal decision.
fable.s: any interest earned and payable on such bonds by the date of conversion is an eligible cost of construction

opus.w: This provision only decides which costs (interest on bonds) count as eligible construction costs for converted Interstate projects. It mentions state and local governments only as bond issuers. They are not consulted or brought into any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking requirement, or right to sue, so the section does not involve participation.
opus.s: for which the proceeds of bonds issued by the State, county, city, or other political subdivision of the State were used, any interest earned and payable on such bonds by the date of conversion is an eligible cost of construction
opus.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: the section names "the State, county, city, or other political subdivision," which might look like outside governments taking part in a federal decision. That reading fails because those entities appear only as the issuers of bonds whose interest can count as a construction cost. No one is consulted, there is no hearing or comment period, no rulemaking is required, and no one gets a right to object or sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines what costs are eligible for federal reimbursement. It mentions state and local governments only as issuers of bonds, not as participants in a decision-making process. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or public input from these outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: For any project under construction on January 1, 1978, on the Interstate System and converted to a regularly funded project after January 1, 1978, for which the proceeds of bonds issued by the State, county, city, or other political subdivision of the State were used, any interest earned and payable on such bonds by the date of conversion is an eligible cost of construction, to the extent that the proceeds of such bonds have actually been expended in the construction of such projects.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "State, county, city, or other political subdivision," it involves outside entities. However, the text merely defines financial eligibility criteria for federal reimbursement. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from these local entities before making a decision. The local entities are simply the issuers of bonds whose interest is being counted as a cost. There is no participatory process (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory role) described here.
